name: D1X Mod 3

parties.name: Intel
parties.note: Intel's technology development group runs its Oregon R&D fabs, which Intel says take each new process from development to high-volume production.

summary: The third module of Intel's D1X fab in Hillsboro, Oregon, which Intel calls a development factory. Construction started in 2019 and the module opened on 11 April 2022 after an investment of more than $3 billion, adding about 270,000 square feet of cleanroom that Intel said was for developing next-generation process technologies. At the opening Intel renamed the campus Gordon Moore Park at Ronler Acres. Local press describes D1X as the factory where Intel develops new chips and begins their high-volume production, which then continues at other Intel sites, and Intel's 2025 annual report says its Oregon fabs take each new process to high-volume production and also run high-volume manufacturing, with Oregon ramping Intel 18A in 2025, without naming individual fabs.

location.site: Gordon Moore Park at Ronler Acres

metrics.note: Added cleanroom space; Intel officials told local press it was a 20% increase.

sources.title: Intel Opens Factory Expansion in Oregon, Renames Site for Gordon Moore
At unveiling of $3 billion Oregon expansion, Intel CEO calls for federal semiconductor action

notes: D1X is primarily a technology development fab, and Intel's opening release describes Mod 3 only as development space. It is kept in scope, rather than excluded as research-only, because local press reports that Intel begins high-volume production at D1X (s2) and Intel's 2025 annual report says its Oregon fabs carry new processes to high-volume production and also perform high-volume manufacturing (s3). Neither source says which products Mod 3 itself makes.
